outcome: admission to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: The study included 50 preeclampsia patients and 50 healthy normotensive pregnant women followed up in a tertiary gynecology and obstetrics center.
finding: Newborns of preeclamptic mothers had significantly lower mean gestational age and Apgar scores, longer hospitalization, and a higher incidence of various perinatal complications including NICU admission, asphyxia, RDS, convulsions, intracranial hemorrhage, jaundice, anemia, and infection.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was significantly more frequent in preeclampsia than in the normal pregnancy group.
